title: Crestline POC - weekly network & routing stability handoff
topics: egress shaping and MTU mismatch troubleshooting
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on network-induced tail latency. SE presented traces showing egress bursts to the private VPC peering and a small number of requests overflowing primary route. Team agreed on a short canary for kernel upgrade with a rollback window, finalize MTU alignment, and run a 30m synthetic load during an agreed maintenance window. Next steps: Redwood to provide telemetry workbook and a small trace bundle, Crestline to validate MTU on firewalls and schedule maintenance window.
next_steps: Redwood: share narrowed trace bundle + telemetry workbook (Alyssa) - due 2027-11-05
Customer: confirm maintenance window and on-call rotation for 2027-11-10 02:00-03:00 UTC (Tom) - due 2027-11-07
Redwood SE: prepare kernel rollback playbook and canary config (Marco) - due 2027-11-08
Customer NetEng: validate MTU and report any mid-path fragmentation (Priya) - due 2027-11-06
action_items: Alyssa Chen: upload trace.zip and telemetry_workbook.xlsx to shared drive and drop link in CRM - due 2027-11-05
Marco Reyes: produce a 1-page rollback playbook + canary config snippet and runbook - due 2027-11-08
Priya Kaur: run MTU traceroutes and capture ICMP fragmentation, attach logs - due 2027-11-06
Tom Nguyen: confirm maintenance window and on-call participants - due 2027-11-07
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-03 16:00 PST / 2027-11-03 23:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alyssa Chen, Marco Reyes - Redwood; Tom Nguyen, Priya Kaur, Jordan Ellis, Ellen Park, Samir Patel - Crestline

[00:00] Alyssa Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick checkin today, i know we all have a lot on our plates. i'll kick off with the headline - Marco found a pattern in the traces that's correlating with the tail latency upticks last week.
[00:28] Marco Reyes: yeah uh hi, yeah so i pulled the kube-proxy egress traces plus the redwood runtime spans, and the common bit is a small set of flows that go to the primary egress peer and we see queueing at the customer border - looks like periodic bursts every ~5-8 minutes.
[00:46] Priya Kaur: sorry can you say "border" again? you mean the firewall on our edge?
[00:49] Marco Reyes: yes, the firewall / edge peer. the packets are queuing there, we see retransmits, and then downstream the redwood instance's KV cache - so the tail gets worse because of KV cache misses for long-lived chat sessions.
[01:12] Jordan Ellis: hmm i wonder if mtu mismatch is playing a part, we had a recent change to jumbo frames in the datacenter last month.
[01:19] Marco Reyes: that's possible - in a couple of traces we saw icmp fragmentation and DF flags. there was one path where mtu looked like 1400 instead of 1500, so fragmentation triggered and then reassembly delays.
[01:32] Priya Kaur: we do have a downstream link that terminates on a 1400 MTU appliance, yeah i'll check that.
[01:38] Tom Nguyen: are these bursts coming from load spikes or are they internal? like is it Redwood sending heavy parallel requests?
[01:44] Marco Reyes: good question. from our telemetry the request pattern is steady; the bursts line up with periodic background syncs from Crestline's internal analytics service—looks like 1-2 large batched requests that coincide with egress saturation.
[01:59] Samir Patel: oh right that nightly analytics job was reconfigured to run every 6 minutes by mistake, that explains the cadence.
[02:06] Alyssa Chen: ok that is a great find — so two prongs: Crestline to fix or reschedule the analytics job, and Redwood to make routing more graceful and to add a canary for the kernel/quant update so we don't worsen the tail.
[02:20] Ellen Park: security question — any of this touching PII in the traces? we need to ensure we don't move PHI outside the VPC for compliance.
[02:27] Marco Reyes: good call, the trace bundle we'll share is sanitized, we redact payloads and PII. we'll only include headers, timing, and span ids.
[02:34] Ellen Park: please add that to the workbook and mark redacted.
[02:38] Alyssa Chen: noted, we'll include a redaction note and the scope of fields.
[02:42] [brief pause] 
[02:50] Marco Reyes: jumping to the kernel/quant upgrade — we rolled the new quant kernels to a small canary in our staging yesterday and saw a small improvement in median but an increase in 99.9th in a couple of runs, likely due to longer kernel init on cold paths.
[03:06] Priya Kaur: so is the plan to go ahead with the upgrade during the pilot? i'm worried about unknowns on our side.
[03:10] Marco Reyes: we want to try a controlled canary in production during a maintenance window with explicit rollback. the canary will target 5% of traffic to a dedicated pool; if tail latency exceeds thresholds for three consecutive 5-minute windows we auto-roll back.
[03:25] Tom Nguyen: that sounds reasonable, what thresholds are you thinking?
[03:29] Marco Reyes: for this workload let's set 99th < 550ms and 99.9th < 900ms; if exceeded trigger rollback. also we have circuit-breaker fallback to a smaller quantized variant which is a lower-throughput but more predictable path.
[03:45] Jordan Ellis: is that fallback an entirely different model or just a runtime mode?
[03:49] Marco Reyes: runtime mode: different kernel path + quant profile. not model-level. should be transparent to app but metrics will show the change.
[03:56] Samir Patel: how quick is rollback? can we avoid a full cold restart?
[04:00] Marco Reyes: rollback is immediate at the routing layer — traffic shifts off the canary pool within seconds, but cold cache misses will take a few minutes to warm back up on the stable pool, so expect transient tail noise for 5-10 minutes after rollback.
[04:13] Alyssa Chen: important to plan the observation window then. we should do the canary during a maintenance window so your on-call can watch and we can accept the transient warmup.
[04:23] Priya Kaur: okay, i'll coordinate the 02:00-03:00 UTC slot next week.
[04:28] Tom Nguyen: do we have any automated runbook for MTU or fragmentation detection that we can run before the canary?
[04:34] Marco Reyes: we can provide a small script that does progressive MTU discovery and runs a traceroute with DF set, returns fragmentation metrics. i'll add it to the workbook.
[04:42] Priya Kaur: that would be perfect.
[04:45] [crosstalk briefly]
[04:50] Alyssa Chen: let's talk telemetry - Jordan you mentioned earlier the REDWOOD dashboard showed intermittent spikes, can you pull the exact timestamps?
[04:58] Jordan Ellis: yeah i have them, 2027-11-01 04:12:14 UTC, 04:18:22 UTC, and 04:24:28 UTC, all with elevated p99 beyond baseline.
[05:09] Marco Reyes: those line up with the analytics syncs sample we saw. we'll attach the span ids in the bundle so you can correlate.
[05:16] Ellen Park: also, audit logs — i want to confirm all changes will be tracked and we get an S3-stored activity log for the canary period.
[05:24] Alyssa Chen: yes we can configure the audit exports for that window and give you a signed link for retention.
[05:29] Tom Nguyen: perfect. what about fallback routing? we talked months ago about multi-path routing for this account. can we enable a second egress path as a soft fallback?
[05:39] Marco Reyes: technically yes — we can route to a secondary peer in another POP or a lower-cost zone. it's already in the routing policy, but currently the primary has higher priority. we can tweak the policy to pre-warm the secondary and make it eligible when metrics degrade.
[05:52] Priya Kaur: does that require BGP changes on our side?
[05:55] Marco Reyes: no BGP change; this is on Redwood's side at the overlay routing layer. we will, however, need to ensure the secondary's egress path meets your compliance constraints.
[06:06] Samir Patel: one more thing — we saw a few 502s during the spikes, was that upstream timeouts or internal?
[06:12] Marco Reyes: those 502s correspond to backend timeouts caused by the egress queuing; the runtime's request queue hit the saturation threshold and started returning 502s. we've got a circuit breaker but it was triggered late. we'll move the circuit breaker threshold earlier for this customer and tune the queue depth.
[06:26] Alyssa Chen: action - Marco to provide suggested queue thresholds and breaker values; Priya to run MTU checks; Alyssa to share sanitized traces.
[06:37] Marco Reyes: i'll drop a canary config gist and a rollback playbook to the shared folder after this call. the rollback playbook includes exact CLI snippets and monitoring queries to trigger manual rollback if needed.
[06:50] Tom Nguyen: what about user-facing impact tolerance — our product team says no more than 5 minutes of degraded experience for critical flows.
[06:59] Marco Reyes: with the quick route-switching and a canary cap at 5% we expect to contain impact within that 5-10 minute warmup window; if anything looks off we'll abort the canary earlier.
[07:12] Priya Kaur: will Redwood be on the bridge during the canary?
[07:15] Alyssa Chen: yes we'll have an SE on the bridge and a dedicated Slack channel for rapid comms.
[07:21] Jordan Ellis: good. also request that all retained logs be time-synced to NTP, last time we had clock skew that made trace correlation harder.
[07:29] Marco Reyes: noted, we'll include NTP check steps in the pre-run checklist.
[07:34] [silence for a second] 
[07:40] Ellen Park: small compliance ask: can we get a signed attestation that no plaintext payloads left the VPC in the traces?
[07:48] Alyssa Chen: yes we'll include a short attestation statement in the workbook and the redaction log.
[07:53] Tom Nguyen: ok recap — Crestline: reschedule analytics job and run MTU checks; Redwood: upload traces (redacted), MTU script, queue breaker suggestions, canary + rollback runbook; agree maintenance window 02:00-03:00 UTC next Wednesday pending Tom confirmation.
[08:11] Alyssa Chen: perfect. any other questions?
[08:14] Samir Patel: one quick ask — can we run a short synthetic 30-minute load before the canary to reproduce the pattern?
[08:19] Marco Reyes: yes we can coordinate a synthetic load from our staging agents against your test gateway. recommended pattern: two-minute ramps to 80% then steady state for 20 minutes, then cool down. we'll provide the script.
[08:31] Priya Kaur: sounds good. i'll need the agent IPs whitelisted.
[08:36] Alyssa Chen: noted, we'll send the IP list.
[08:39] [closing remarks] Alyssa Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the trace bundle and the workbook, Marco will post the rollback doc, and Tom will confirm the window. Alyssa signing off.
[08:52] Tom Nguyen: thanks all.

End of transcript.
